title: Google Docs
description: Google Docs as the signed-in Workspace user: read, create, and edit documents by id — Staff meeting notes

guide.summary: Docs by id: tabs, UTF-16 edit indexes, revisions and partial-create recovery.
guide.content:
# Google Docs usage

Purpose: Staff meeting notes

Workspace delegation is configured by the deployment. Each call acts as the mapped Workspace user; document access follows that user's Drive sharing.

## Find the document first

Document ids join Docs to Drive: take the part after `/d/` in a document URL,
or find the file by name through a Google Drive connection. An id the person
provides works as is. Docs has no
account-data search or listing; its operation search discovers API methods.
A missing document may be absent or inaccessible to the mapped Workspace user.

## Read before editing

The rendering follows document tabs, including nested tabs. Headers, footers,
floating images and comments are not rendered; `notRendered` names omitted
kinds. Suggested insertions and deletions can appear together without marks.
An accepted or rejected suggestions preview cannot supply edit indexes.
Indexed rows page with `page.nextCursor`; keep the same arguments, starting
with `maxChars: 0` when only indexes are needed.

Use the inline view's UTF-16 start/end indexes and revision to plan edits.
Indexes shift after each edit, including earlier requests in the same atomic
batch. Apply independent deletions from the end backwards. A revision is a
precondition, never an idempotency key. Re-read and recompute after a revision
conflict.

Styles, named ranges, headers and footers live in the complete document
resource. Read it with
`docs_api_read({path:"/documents/doc_123",query:{includeTabsContent:true}})`
when a rendering cannot answer the task. Paths omit `/v1`; the hatch reply is
`{status,data}`, with the vendor document in `data` (a program call's
`delivery.data.data`). A Docs
create payload sets a title only; initial text is a separate edit. Appending
joins the final paragraph, so begin with a newline when a new paragraph is
intended. A broad text replacement can rewrite every tab.
Batch kinds include `updateTextStyle` for formatting, `insertTable`,
`createParagraphBullets`, and `deleteContentRange`.

## Recover a partial create

If creation succeeded but initial text failed, keep the created document id.
Append the missing text directly only when the failure proves Google refused
it. Otherwise read that document and add only what is missing. Creating again
would make another document. If the create reply lost its id, search Drive for
the title before attempting a fresh create.

Preview comment and suggestion mutations are unavailable. Comments belong to
Drive. Copying a template or choosing a destination folder also belongs to
Drive; a Docs create starts in My Drive's root.

## Conventions

- **Paging:** while `page.hasMore` is true, continue with `page.nextCursor` unchanged. For `docs_api_details`, `docs_api_search`, `get_document`, pass it as the top-level `cursor`; omit raw paging anchors on continuations. Keep the original method, path, filters, page size, fields and headers. The last page has no `nextCursor`. If `page.hasMore` is true without a cursor, the data is incomplete and continuation was withheld. When approaching execute_code's per-program call limit, return page.nextCursor before the call that would exceed it and continue in the next program; don't restart.
- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `docs_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `docs_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `docs_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `docs_api_write` calls a reviewed write; the host may ask the user to confirm it. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. An unknown id, or one these credentials cannot reach, fails as `connector_call_failed`; this API does not tell the two apart. `conflict` means: A revision-guarded batch update returned ABORTED or FAILED_PRECONDITION with HTTP 400 or 409; The document content or revision changed during indexed content paging.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Get one Google Doc as readable markdown-ish text per tab, with its title and revisionId; withIndexes adds the start/end indexes edits target. Cannot search or list documents.

documentId.description: Document id: the part after /d/ in its URL, or a Drive file id for a Google Doc.

tabId.description: Render only this tab (from a previous get_document); omit for every tab.

maxChars.description: Characters of text kept across all rendered tabs, 0 to 1000000; defaults to 20000. Connecta's cap. Longer text ends with a truncation marker. Above the default, call directly (call_tool, connecta.result to page): execute_code carries at most 256 KiB per result.

withIndexes.description: Add each tab's elements: every paragraph, table, and table of contents with UTF-16 startIndex and endIndex, 64 KiB per page (connecta's cap); page with cursor.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the previous indexed read; keep the same arguments and document revision.

suggestions.description: How suggested edits read: inline (editors' default; the indexes edits use), or a preview with all accepted or all rejected (indexes not valid for edits).

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result. Page and truncation metadata are always returned.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new Google Doc in the user's My Drive root with a title and optional plain-text body. Cannot choose a folder, apply a template, or copy a document.

title.description: Document title, one line. Connecta's 1,000-character cap.

text.description: Optional plain-text body; \n starts a new paragraph.

tools.name: append_text
tools.description: Append plain text to the end of a Google Doc's body, or of one tab. It joins the last paragraph; start with \n for a new one. Never removes or restyles text.

documentId.description: Document id: the part after /d/ in its URL, or a Drive file id for a Google Doc.

text.description: Plain text; \n starts a new paragraph. Google caps a document near 1.02 million characters.

tabId.description: Tab to append to; omit for the first tab.

requiredRevisionId.description: revisionId from get_document or a previous edit. If the document has changed since, the edit fails conflict and nothing is applied.

tools.name: insert_text
tools.description: Insert plain text at one UTF-16 index of a Google Doc's body, from get_document withIndexes. Inserts only; nothing existing is removed or restyled.

documentId.description: Document id: the part after /d/ in its URL, or a Drive file id for a Google Doc.

index.description: UTF-16 index inside an existing paragraph, from get_document withIndexes; 1 is the body's start. Not a table's start index.

text.description: Plain text; \n starts a new paragraph. Google caps a document near 1.02 million characters.

tabId.description: Tab the index belongs to; omit for the first tab.

requiredRevisionId.description: revisionId from get_document or a previous edit. If the document has changed since, the edit fails conflict and nothing is applied.

tools.name: replace_all_text
tools.description: Replace every occurrence of a string (or regex) in a Google Doc, in all tabs or the listed ones, and report how many changed. Overwrites text; no preview.

documentId.description: Document id: the part after /d/ in its URL, or a Drive file id for a Google Doc.

find.description: Text to find. With regex: true, a regular expression in Google's RE2 syntax.

replaceWith.description: Replacement text; an empty string deletes every match.

matchCase.description: Match case exactly. Defaults to false.

regex.description: Treat find as an RE2 regular expression. Defaults to false.

tabIds.description: Only these tabs; omit for every tab.

requiredRevisionId.description: revisionId from get_document or a previous edit. If the document has changed since, the edit fails conflict and nothing is applied.

tools.name: batch_update_document
tools.description: Apply raw Docs API documents.batchUpdate requests to one Google Doc at a required revision, atomically: all apply or none. Always destructive; prefer named edits.

documentId.description: Document id: the part after /d/ in its URL, or a Drive file id for a Google Doc.

requests.description: Requests in order, 1 to 100 (connecta's cap). Later requests see earlier ones' index shifts.

requiredRevisionId.description: revisionId from get_document or a previous edit; required, so raw edits are planned against what was read. If the document has changed, it fails conflict and nothing is applied.

tools.name: docs_api_search
tools.description: Find Google Docs API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; docs_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: docs_api_details
tools.description: Read one Google Docs API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: docs_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Google Docs API read. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /documents/doc_123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

tools.name: docs_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed Google Docs API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. Batch updates require writeControl.requiredRevisionId, 1–100 requests and exactly one supported GA kind each; preview comment and suggestion kinds are refused.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /documents/doc_123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
